entities.name: Wang Ch'ung-hui
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Wang Chonghui (1881-12-01, Hong Kong - 1958-03-15) was a prominent Chinese jurist, diplomat, and politician who played a crucial role in shaping the Republic of China's legal and international frameworks. 

 As a close associate of Sun Yat-sen, the republic's founding father, Wang Chonghui served as a judge on the Permanent Court of International Justice in the Hague, contributing to the development of international law. 

 His work in the judiciary and diplomacy had a lasting impact on the governance of the Republic of China, as he helped to establish the country's legal system and negotiate key international agreements. 

 Despite facing significant challenges during the Chinese Civil War, Wang Chonghui's contributions to the Republic of China's legal and political landscape remain an essential part of its history, reflecting his commitment to the principles of democracy and international cooperation. 

 "The Constitution is the greatest achievement of our revolution," Wang Chonghui once said, highlighting his dedication to the cause of democracy and human rights.
